capture.final_message:
Use the quotient representation of double cosets as the central mechanism. First establish the two standard characterizations:

- \(x\sim y\) precisely when \(y=axb\) for some \(a\in H\) and \(b\in K\).
- \(a\in\operatorname{quotToDoubleCoset}(i)\) precisely when \(\operatorname{mk}(a)=i\).

Both sides of the first displayed `Iff` are therefore independently true, so its two implications can ignore their hypotheses.

For the second `Iff`, prove the representative identity
\[
\operatorname{mk}(\operatorname{Quotient.out}(q))=q
\]
from the basic quotient API. Then show that the quotient is finite exactly when finitely many of its fibers cover \(G\):

- If the quotient is finite, take the finset of all quotient classes; their associated double cosets cover \(G\).
- Conversely, if a finite finset \(I\) of classes covers \(G\), apply the cover to \(\operatorname{Quotient.out}(q)\). The membership characterization gives \(q=i\) for some \(i\in I\), using the representative identity. Thus every quotient class lies in \(I\), yielding finiteness.

Again, both propositions in that `Iff` are established outright; the outer equivalence is then assembled formally.
